name: meeple-on-board-per-meeple-v1
description: ⚠️ 09/09/2026, THE COMMONS FLIP: THIS ARM NOW PINS THE PASSENGERS AS WELL. Dean ruled the commons in as the engine DEFAULT (docs/commons-handoff-2026-09-09-v1.md), which moved four leaves at once - rules.turn.visitCurrency to 'commons', rules.turn.bonusTiming to 'start', rules.turn.startingMeeplesPerColour to 0, and the Orchard door's printed draw to 2/2. An overlay that pins only what it is named for stops being the arm it is called, silently, which is the 05/09/2026 lesson written down: NAME THE PASSENGERS BEFORE RULING AN ARM IN. So the `set` below carries every leaf this arm's game relied on, whether or not it was in the original experiment. R17 with a host chosen PER MEEPLE rather than per payment, so one payment may feed several neighbours. Identical to overlays/meeple-on-board-v1.overlay.json in every other respect. It is the rule Dean ruled first on 05/09/2026 and then ruled back on the branching factor, and it survives as the paired arm that says what the ruling cost in play: per meeple multiplies the build enumerator by roughly hosts^meeples and measured at 25,827 ways to buy one building at four seats against 4,063 per payment, with seconds per 4-seat game 0.277 against 0.152. Run it to find out whether the freedom bought anything at the table - the readings to compare are who receives placed meeples (the spread across seats) and the hook. ⛔ PASSENGERS PINNED 12/09/2026: Dean's plain-action balloon and Village Store ruling moved sixteen shipped leaves at once. This overlay predates that flip and every report taken against it does too, so each of those leaves is pinned here BY NAME at its PRE-FLIP value. Without it an arm read as a delta against a pre-flip base would silently gain a one-card flight, an always-present Aerodrome and a live coin economy. That is the 05/09/2026 passenger lesson: an overlay that should not move with the shipped default has to pin every knob the flip moved.
